long_biography.plain_text:
Blake Sartini began on the casino floor at Station Casinos and rose through its operations, eventually becoming chief operating officer. While there, he co-founded the Southwest slot-machine route. In 2001 he acquired that subsidiary in exchange for Station shares he held, creating the platform for Golden Gaming. The business grew beyond slot routes into Nevada gaming taverns and casino properties, and Golden Entertainment became the public-company successor with Sartini as chairman and chief executive. The share exchange showed an operator using an existing equity stake to pursue a business he understood from its beginnings.

Golden returned to private family ownership in 2026 through a transaction involving Sartini and VICI Properties. VICI acquired the real estate of seven casino resorts and leased it to Sartini-controlled entities, while Golden retained operations. The company now describes a portfolio of eight casinos and 73 Nevada gaming taverns. Sartini's wife, Delise Fertitta Sartini, was also identified by regulators as a controlling beneficial owner during the public-company period; their son Blake L. Sartini II is a separate executive who serves as chief operating officer.
